title: An algebra of infinite little finitistic dimension
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the finitistic dimension conjecture: a finite-dimensional complex algebra A with finite-dimensional modules N_m whose projective dimensions are finite and at least 2m - 2, so that findim A = Findim A = infinity. The course proves the radical theory, projective covers and minimal resolutions it uses; builds a finitely presented group algebra with a selection process of unbounded extinction; encodes its presentation in a three-vertex algebra B of global dimension two; inverts two arrows in a Verdier quotient and replaces a missing summand by an odd double; clears the denominators of a finite diagram; packs the chain maps and homotopies into one three-column complex of B-bimodules that realizes the selection; simulates it by an ordinary bimodule over a product algebra; and turns iterates into projective dimension with the bar decomposition of a trivial extension. A corollary, under named results of Cummings and Rickard, gives an algebra whose finitistic dimensions are infinite on the left and zero on the right.
prerequisites: core course Graduate Algebra (Li, Methods of Algebra, Volume 1): semisimple modules (Proposition 6.11.4); finitely generated modules over a principal ideal domain (Theorem 6.7.8, used in an exercise)

core course Category Theory and Homological Methods (Li, Methods of Algebra, Volume 2): Tor (Definition-Proposition 3.14.7); truncation (Definition 3.9.3, Proposition 3.9.8); exactness of row-exact double complexes (Corollary 3.10.7); Gabriel-Zisman localization by roofs (Theorem 1.9.11, Corollary 1.9.13); triangulated categories, cohomological Hom functors and split triangles (Proposition 4.1.12, Remark 4.1.11, Corollary 4.1.13, Proposition 4.2.6); the homotopy category and induced triangulated functors (Theorem 4.4.1, Corollaries 4.4.2 and 4.4.4, Propositions 4.4.3 and 4.4.7); Verdier localization (Propositions 4.3.2 and 4.3.3, Theorem 4.3.4); Ext in the derived category and projective dimension (Definition 4.5.8, Proposition 4.5.9, Proposition 4.9.6, Definition-Proposition 4.9.7); K-flat complexes and derived tensor products (Propositions 4.12.4, 4.12.9 and 4.12.13)
programme course Van Kampen diagrams (van-kampen-diagrams): Words, free groups and Cayley graphs, Lemma 1.2 and Section 2 (free groups and presented groups)

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof, only in Corollary 5.1 of the last lesson (the left-right asymmetry): (CUM) Cummings, Left-right symmetry of finite finitistic dimension, arXiv:2211.04394, Construction 2.1 and Propositions 3.2, 3.3, 4.3 and 4.4 (finitistic dimensions and injective generation for the triangular algebra attached to a basic algebra over an algebraically closed field); (RIC) Rickard, Unbounded derived categories and the finitistic dimension conjecture, arXiv:1804.09801, Theorem 4.3 (injective generation implies finite big finitistic dimension); (MOR) every finite-dimensional algebra is Morita equivalent to a basic one, and Morita equivalence preserves finite generation, projective dimension, injective modules and coproducts in the unbounded derived category (core course Category Theory and Homological Methods, Li, Volume 2, Section 7.7, for Morita theory; the existence of a basic algebra is not proved there). The main theorem (lesson 8, Theorem 4.1) uses none of them.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
